classes.note: First past the post in single-member constituencies (63 since 2011). Parliament lasts five years from its first sitting unless dissolved sooner, and a general election follows each dissolution (Constitution s.64). The 2025 election was the 19th under universal adult suffrage, introduced in 1944.

classes.name: Referendums
classes.note: The only referendum so far is that of 19 September 1961 on staying in the Federation of the West Indies, held under the colonial government. The Constitution requires a referendum for a bill altering its deeply entrenched provisions (s.49); none has been held since independence.

dates.note: Federation referendum; the date is not quoted from a fetched official source.

classes.name: Elections in Jamaica to the House of Representatives of the West Indies Federation
classes.name_en: West Indies Federation House of Representatives (Jamaica seats)
classes.note: Jamaica returned 17 of the 45 members of the federal House at the only federal election, 25 March 1958; the Federation was dissolved on 31 May 1962. Not quoted from a fetched official source.

dates.note: The only federal general election; the date is not quoted from a fetched official source.

classes.name: Elections of members of the Legislative Council
classes.note: Under crown colony government an elected minority of the Legislative Council was chosen by a property and tax franchise, one member per parish from 1895; replaced by the House of Representatives under the 1944 Constitution.
classes.disposition_reason: Returns were printed only in the Jamaica Gazette and colonial blue books; no official publication of them is online, and the ECJ's listings start in 1944.

classes.name: Elections to the House of Assembly of Jamaica
classes.note: The elected assembly of the colony, chosen by freeholders under a property franchise, surrendered its powers after the Morant Bay rebellion and was abolished, and crown colony government began in 1866.
classes.disposition_reason: Polls survive only in the Assembly's journals and parish records; no official body publishes results.

classes.name: The Senate
classes.disposition_reason: The Senate is appointed, not elected: 13 senators on the advice of the Prime Minister and 8 on the advice of the Leader of the Opposition (Constitution s.35).

classes.name: Governor-General and Prime Minister
classes.disposition_reason: The Governor-General is appointed by the monarch, and the Prime Minister is appointed from the House as the member best able to command its majority (Constitution ss.27 and 70); neither is chosen by a public vote.

classes.name: Judges
classes.disposition_reason: Judges and resident magistrates are appointed by the Governor-General, on the advice of the Prime Minister or the Judicial Service Commission (Constitution Chapter VII); none is elected.

classes.name: Party candidate selections
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their candidates by their own delegates' conferences; the state neither runs nor publishes them, and candidates enter the official process only at nomination day.

classes.name: Local government elections of councillors
classes.name_en: Municipal corporation councillors (parish councils and KSAC before 2016)
classes.finest_note: Councillors are elected in single-member electoral divisions; the ECJ counts each division by polling station, but division results files have not been reached for this census.
classes.note: First past the post in single-member electoral divisions (228 since at least 2012) for the 13 municipal corporations (the parish councils and the Kingston and St. Andrew Corporation before the Local Governance Act 2016) and the Portmore municipality. Elections have repeatedly been postponed by Act of Parliament.
